inputs.input: I choose Mage.
I pick Arcane Bolt and Flame Lance.
I walk toward the city gates of Glassmere.
I join the queue and, when it's my turn, ask the guard where a new mage can find the adventurer's guild.
I follow the guard's directions down Gate Street, past the fountain, left at the fork, and look for the timber-framed building with the sword and branch over its door.
I step inside, ring the bell, and ask the clerk to register me as a new adventurer.
I pay the two silver, say "Alaric Red," and touch the measuring stone.
"Tell me more about Glimmerdeep — what do the crystal and beetle parts fetch, and is there anything dangerous past the outer grottos?" I also glance at the notice board for any low-tier contracts.

f.t8.m16.d2_2.1.o: Holm the jeweler in town buys beetle crystal by the ounce; clear pieces fetch a few coppers each, cloudy ones less

f.t8.m16.d3_3.1.o: the academy pays a small bounty per crystal slime body (as of last season), since the slimes foul their leaching vats

f.t8.m16.d4_4.1.o: an old crystal archway across the main passage marks the limit of the outer grottos; the deep galleries beyond are the academy's own and off-limits to the Guild

f.t8.m16.d5_5.1.o: the rock near the stream is slick; beetles run when hurt, slimes are slow and stupid

f.t9.m18.d1.1.o: North from the Guild hall via the market square and north road; at the fork past the sheep pens take the left fork to keep the valley; the stream runs out of the cleft; a morning's walk for most

f.t9.m18.d4_2.1.o: The clerk says a torch and a bite of bread is all a beetle cull wants; the grottos aren't dark but the corners are

f.t9.m18.d5_3.1.o: There is a water trough by the north gate worth filling a skin at; the academy's pipes run near the cleft stream and they take it ill when folk drink their runoff

f.t12.m24.d3.1.o: Holm the jeweler buys beetle crystal by the ounce — clear pieces a few coppers each, cloudy less; he has no use for shells or legs; herb folk on Tanner's Row sometimes want carapace for pennies; the a

f.t14.m28.d2.1.o: Visitors must stay this side of the crystal line (arch and columns), outer grottos only, six down at most; whatever is killed is the killer's own.

f.t14.m28.d3_2.1.o: Slime bodies fetch a bounty at the academy; beetles are sold by the crystal.

f.t14.m28.d4_3.1.o: counted Alaric in at the gate ledger around half eleven

f.t15.m36.d1.1.o: A broad swept band of grit along the near wall pocked with dozens of fresh three-toed marks, all heading into a low crack in the far wall

f.t24.m54.d4.1.o: any of the inns will feed breakfast for a copper more if asked the night before

f.t25.m58.d4_2.1.o: the water tastes of the pipe

f.t27.m62.d4_4.1.o: a mage with a Guild plate; Holm has been talking about the crystal he brought him

f.t27.m62.d7_5.1.o: something in the college cold stores eats through sacks and gnaws through oak, fouling ale casks; stewards won't pay an exterminator until after the harvest feast; Wren thinks rats, Dace doubts it

f.t28.m64.d2.1.o: calls the college cellars the undercrofts and warns they run under the old wall

f.t28.m64.d4_2.1.o: can take Alaric to the college cellars now, a ten-minute walk past the chapel, to see the torn-open sacks

f.t29.m66.d1.1.o: eight silver when the creature is dead and they have seen it

f.t30.m68.d3_3.1.o: past full dark, a heavy weight dragged against stone at the far end by the old wall, and grain being pushed through the scattered barley

f.t30.m68.d4_4.1.o: two dull green eyes, low to the ground and set wide apart, opened in the dark at the far end and went still

f.t31.m72.d2_2.1.o: eats grain, roots and bark; not a man-eater; will charge if pressed (Wren)

f.t32.m74.d1.1.o: smoke and a way out: the grave-borer dug under the wall from the churchyard side after the autumn rains; seal its way in and it panics, leave it a door and it takes it

f.t32.m74.d2_2.1.o: a hole at the base of the wall behind the beast, where the stone ribs meet the floor — the way the grave-borer dug in

f.t32.m74.d3_3.1.o: mouth closed partway, hiss thinned to a slow breath, head turned toward the dark wall behind it, checking its own exit

f.t32.m74.d4_4.1.o: cleared his borer with smoke — wet straw, green wood, a boy with a bellows — and it went up through its own tunnel; took an evening

f.t32.m74.d5_5.1.o: smoke it up and out, or block the tunnel after and take it the hard way; steward's silver near enough the same either way

f.t32.m74.d6_6.1.o: would rather kill the beast than let it walk; it has eaten half their barley

f.t33.m76.d2.1.o: up to the kitchen yard for green wood and spoiled straw from the stable end, then returned with both

f.t33.m76.d3_2.1.o: the bellows from the bake-house and a clay fire-pot

f.t33.m76.d4_3.1.o: a dug opening behind it at the base of the old wall, wide as a bread oven's mouth, packed earth rimmed with root-hair, half-hidden by a fallen rib of wall

f.t33.m76.d6_5.1.o: rose off its belly, breathing fast, waiting at the lip of its burrow to see what the smoke meant

f.t33.m76.d7_6.1.o: back down in the cold stores with straw and green hazel, sleeve over his nose, waiting on Alaric's hand for the lighting

f.t33.m76.d8_7.1.o: a few paces off Alaric's shoulder holding the bellows mouth ready, fire piled against the stair-side wall far from the tunnel end

f.t34.m78.d2_2.1.o: smoke drove it into its tunnel; it dug away beneath the chapel yard

f.t35.m80.d2.1.o: packed tight with mortared rubble and tamped earth; holds against Dace's shoves

f.t35.m80.d5_3.1.o: will bring Alaric to the Steward at first light to have the eight silver counted out from the Steward's purse

f.t38.m86.d2_2.1.o: the packed wall in the cold stores and allowed it solid work that will hold until masons open the floor proper

f.t38.m86.d3_3.1.o: eight silver coins on his desk, lined in a row, held back pending Alaric's account of the crystal Master Holm has been going on about

f.t39.m88.d2.1.o: a man who does solid work and tells a straight story — will call on him if the wall troubles him before the college pays for masons

last.input: "Back to the Guild," I say. "A paid mage needs better work than lost goats." I thank Dace for the bread and head for the Guild hall to see what the board offers.

inputs.input: "Keep the lantern low and stay by the stair," I say. I set a torch ready by the cask shelf, then eat a handful of travel biscuits while we wait for the scraping to come back.
I raise the torch high and advance slowly toward the green eyes, trying to force the creature to show itself.

"It doesn't want a fight, and neither do I at full strength," I say without turning. "Wren — how did your uncle clear his? Smoke, noise, digging it a way out? I'd rather chase it off than bleed for eight silver."
"Smoke it up and out, then we block the tunnel after," I say. "Dace — wet straw and green wood? Wren, you mentioned a bellows."
I light the straw and green wood and step back toward the stair with the others, letting the draught carry the smoke to the tunnel.
"Pack it now, then," I say. I help Dace ram the rubble stones tight into the tunnel mouth and tamp earth behind them until the wall holds solid.
"First light works," I say. "Until then, is there a corner out of the cold where a mage can sleep a few hours? I'll want my wits about me when your Steward counts slow."
I settle onto the bench by the hearth and sleep until Dace wakes me at first light.
"Ready," I say, and follow Dace up to the Steward's chamber for my eight silver.
I tell him plainly: the crystal came out of the flooded cellar dig, Master Holm examined it, and it's lodged with the Guild now — I can fetch the clerk's receipt if he wants it in writing.
I take the eight silver, thank him, and follow Dace down for the warm bread.
"Back to the Guild," I say. "A paid mage needs better work than lost goats." I thank Dace for the bread and head for the Guild hall to see what the board offers.
